question: In the pyrolysis of oil shale kerogen, by how many degrees does the maximum of the H2 signal occur earlier under air than under nitrogen?
expect: about 120 C: maximum near 330 C in air vs near 450 C in nitrogen (sec. 3.3.1)
trap: the 50 C earlier onset of mass loss

- 2.3.1. TOC Content Testing. The dried rock samples were ground to approximately 120 mesh, and 0.2−0.5 g was weighed into a crucible. To remove carbonate minerals while avoiding excessive acidolysis of organic matter, the samples were treated with dilute hydrochloric acid (1 mol L^− 1) at room temperature for 12 h, followed by a further 2 h treatment with freshly prepared dilute hydrochloric acid of the same concentration. The residue was suction-filtered and washed with distilled water until neutral and free of chloride, as indicated by the absence of AgCl precipitation upon testing the washings with AgNO3 solution. - The reaction purge-gas flow rate was 50 mL min^−1, and the nitrogen protective-gas flow rate was 20 mL min^−1.
- The oil shale powder was sequentially treated with 20% hydrochloric acid and a mixed acid (20% hydrochloric acid and 40% hydrofluoric acid mixed at a volume ratio of 1:2) under a 70 °C water bath condition, alternating stirring multiple times to remove inorganic minerals such as carbonates and silicates.
- The acid-washed samples were washed with deionized water to near neutrality and then placed in a 105 °C oven to dry to a constant weight.
- Upon testing, the loss on ignition (LOI) of the kerogen prepared in this experiment was 88%, satisfying the regulatory requirement of an LOI greater than 75% specified in the national standard.
